8. The naive oversupply proxy (what notebooks 22/36 actually used), and why it’s biased.
Built entirely from observed values — which is exactly the problem, since at the hours with the most curtailment, the observed numerator is already suppressed by that same curtailment.

Realized residual load is a pure accounting identity from already-observed values — nothing to estimate. The forecastable version substitutes gross demand and potential-minus-estimated-curtailment for the observed quantities, so it can be computed ahead of time from weather and calendar alone.

regardless,

makes checkable: it shows wind offshore curtailed roughly 8-9x more
heavily per MW installed than onshore (see the congestion data chapter) —
a real technology-specific asymmetry that the pooled onshore+offshore
curtailment curve in notebooks 39/40/42 currently discards.
